Executive Summary

Aurora is a 184-unit garden-style multifamily asset located in the Sunbelt MSA of Greenville, South Carolina. The sponsor seeks a $24M senior bridge loan to refinance existing CMBS debt and fund $3.2M of light interior renovations.

The property was acquired in 2019 at a basis of $128k/unit. The sponsor has executed on 78% of their original business plan, with in-place rents now $1,425/mo on the renovated units versus $1,180/mo on classics. The remaining 41 classic units present a clear continuation of the same playbook over the next 24 months.

The senior loan structures at a 68% LTV against a third-party appraisal of $35.4M and amortizes interest-only for the 36-month term. Two 12-month extensions are available subject to a DSCR test of 1.20x on trailing 3-month NOI.

The Greenville MSA's median household income has grown from $52,400 in 2018 to $68,900 in 2024, supporting both the rent levels achieved on the renovated stock and the moderate further push the sponsor underwrites on the remaining classic units.

Aurora's rent-to-income ratio at the underwritten stabilized rents sits at 24.1% — well below the 30% affordability ceiling and providing a meaningful cushion against further rate-driven affordability pressure across the Sunbelt.

Sponsor Track Record

Stillwater Partners is a vertically-integrated owner-operator headquartered in Charlotte, NC with $1.1B of AUM across 14 active multifamily properties in the Carolinas, Georgia, and Tennessee. The principals have executed on 27 value-add multifamily projects since 2011, with a realized gross IRR of 24.6% across the seven full-cycle dispositions.

"Stillwater has been our most consistent sponsor in the Carolinas — they buy at the right basis and execute the renovation playbook without surprises."

The sponsor has a 100% guarantee track record with no recourse triggers across 19 prior bridge loans, including two that were extended through the 2022-2023 rate-cycle correction.

Market Overview — Greenville, SC

Greenville has experienced top-decile rent growth among Southeast MSAs over the trailing five years, with effective rents up 41% on a same-store basis. Population growth of 7.8% versus the national average of 2.6% has driven both rent and absorption metrics.

Figure 1. Effective same-store rent index, Greenville-Spartanburg MSA. Source: CoStar.

Forward supply pipeline is moderating: 2025 deliveries are projected at 1,840 units versus a trailing average of 2,650, supportive of continued rent growth in the renovated B-asset segment Aurora occupies.

Employer concentration risk is moderate. The top five employers (Michelin North America, Greenville Health System, Bon Secours St. Francis, BMW Manufacturing, and Lockheed Martin) collectively employ 41,500 across the MSA, with no single employer exceeding 4% of total payrolls.

The Aurora property is situated in the Mauldin-Simpsonville submarket, which has experienced the highest in-migration in the MSA over the trailing 24 months. New single-family permitting in the submarket rose 38% year-over-year, providing a structural demand tailwind for B-quality multifamily product.

Public transit access is limited, but the property is positioned within a 15-minute drive of three of the five top employment centers, supporting durable demand from the core $50-90k household-income renter cohort that Aurora targets.

Lender Comparables

Three recent bridge transactions in the immediate submarket establish a clear pricing floor and credit benchmark for the Aurora opportunity. All three closed within the trailing nine months at LTVs between 65% and 71% and spreads between SOFR + 325 and SOFR + 395.

The most comparable transaction is the November 2024 refinance of Highland Crossing, a 152-unit 2004-vintage value-add bridge that closed at 70% LTV, SOFR + 365, with a 36-month term and a 4.50% strike cap. Aurora prices inside Highland on both LTV and spread reflecting the stronger sponsor track record.

Two additional comparable transactions — Westbrook Commons (133 units, October 2024, 68% LTV, SOFR + 380) and Riverstone Park (201 units, August 2024, 65% LTV, SOFR + 345) — bracket the Aurora pricing within the prevailing market clearing band.

Part II — Risk & Mitigants

Identified Risks

Renovation execution risk: 41 classic units remain. Mitigant: sponsor has completed 143 of 184 renovations on schedule and within $200/unit of budget. The construction line is sized to fully fund remaining scope at $7,800 per unit.

Interest-rate sensitivity: the loan is floating-rate SOFR + 350. Mitigant: a 4.00% SOFR cap is required at closing for the full term, capping the all-in coupon at 7.50%.

Submarket concentration: the sponsor has three other assets within a 12-mile radius. Mitigant: the assets serve distinct rent tiers ($1,050 / $1,425 / $1,890 average rent) and have not historically cannibalized each other.

Insurance pricing exposure: Sunbelt multifamily insurance premiums have risen 18-26% annually since 2022. Mitigant: the underwriting assumes a 22% step-up on renewal and the sponsor has secured a binding indication for the next 24 months at a 19% step-up.

Property tax reassessment risk: South Carolina law caps annual tax growth on owner-occupied homes but not on income-producing real estate. Mitigant: the underwriting reflects a stabilized assessed value 11% above the current assessment with a tax-grievance allowance funded at $80/unit/year.

Conclusion

OKOA's underwriting supports the senior commitment at a 68% LTV. The combination of an experienced sponsor, a top-quartile growth market, a renovated-asset basis, and a fully-funded capex line produces an attractive risk-adjusted opportunity. We recommend approval subject to standard pre-closing diligence.

Appendix A — Glossary

DSCR: Debt Service Coverage Ratio. Calculated as NOI divided by annual debt service.

LTV: Loan-to-Value. Senior loan principal divided by third-party appraised value.

NOI: Net Operating Income. Effective Gross Income less operating expenses, excluding capital expenditures and debt service.

SOFR: Secured Overnight Financing Rate. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York's overnight risk-free reference rate.

[4] Glossary definitions are summary only and not contractual definitions; see the executed loan agreement for binding definitions.
